evals.name: web-build-settings-card
evals.prompt: This NotificationSettings React component works but looks really plain and developer-default. Make it feel premium and polished. Rewrite the component (Tailwind is available) and briefly explain the key changes you made and why.
evals.expected_output: A rewritten React/Tailwind component with real interaction states (hover/active/focus/disabled/loading), 4px-based spacing, refined typography, soft elevation, semantic toggle styling, and a short rationale tying changes to premium-UI principles.

evals.name: mobile-build-login-screen
evals.prompt: Here's a basic Flutter login screen. It functions but feels generic. Make it feel like a high-end, premium app. Give me the improved Dart and call out what you changed.
evals.expected_output: Improved Flutter screen addressing keyboard handling (scroll/avoid inset), press feedback (scale), haptics on submit, loading-in-button, refined spacing/typography, focus/error states, plus a rationale.

evals.name: review-dashboard-premium
evals.prompt: I'm building a dark-mode analytics dashboard in React. Cards, a sidebar, charts, a data table that shows a spinner while loading and 'No results' when empty. It all works but it feels cheap and flat compared to apps like Linear or Vercel. Review my approach and tell me specifically what to change to make it feel premium. I don't have the code handy, just go off the description.
evals.expected_output: A structured premium-UI review: dark-theme depth via lighter surfaces (not shadows), shimmer skeletons instead of spinners, a teaching empty state instead of 'No results', hierarchy/spacing/typography guidance, interaction states, and subtle motion — each finding paired with a concrete fix and reason.

evals.name: mock-tabs-and-way-back
evals.prompt: This is an HTML prototype of a point-of-sale order screen with order tabs: 'Order 1', 'Phone call' and a '+ New' button. The owner pressed '+ New' several times and now asks how to get rid of the empty tabs. Fix the prototype's tab behavior.
evals.expected_output: Classifies tab creation as a 'created' action: '+ New' does not stack empty tabs (goes to the existing empty one), an empty tab disappears when left, the active tab gets a close control with a 44-48 px hit area, closing a tab with content offers Undo, one tab always stays, '+ New' stays outside the scrolling tab row, the active tab scrolls into view; verifies by pressing every control, not by screenshots.

evals.name: payment-short-cash
evals.prompt: Our Flutter till's cash payment screen has quick-sum buttons (207, 250, 500) and if the guest gives less than the total, the cashier has to accept the cash and then start a second payment for the rest. The owner finds it confusing. Redesign the payment step.
evals.expected_output: One payment screen with cash, card, transfer and split; the amount typed on a bottom keypad; change or shortfall shown live in the danger color; the primary button states the result and stays readable when disabled; a short cash amount offers 'Rest by card' that turns the same screen into a split with the cash kept; unlabelled quick sums removed; tabular figures; result screen with the change first that pauses on touch; payment is final (no Undo toast), refund is a separate action.

evals.name: review-interactive-mock
evals.prompt: Review this interactive HTML mock of a delivery dispatch screen before I show it to the owner. Be thorough.
evals.expected_output: Walks the main jobs end to end on phone and desktop sizes, presses every control and reports dead/fake controls and toast-instead-of-process actions, checks that objects persist across screens, growing lists at 1/3/5/15 items, short-screen sheets, way back per action class, variants (offline, roles), measures targets and contrast, separates live checks from code reading, lists what was not checked, and orders findings as classes with shared-layer fixes.

evals.name: sheet-and-gestures
evals.prompt: Add swipe and long-press interactions to our React Native order list: swipe to remove, long press for options, and make the order sheet feel native.
evals.expected_output: Uses one gesture grammar (swipe left removes with Undo, swipe right does the row's main next step, long press opens choices and never acts), each gesture with a visible alternative (WCAG 2.5.1/2.5.7), reveal-under-row feedback with a commit threshold and spring-back, sheet draggable from anywhere when its list is at the top, scrim ignores the opening tap, motion from one module with a spring, haptics mapped by meaning, reduced motion honored.

evals.name: ready-to-ship-verdict
evals.prompt: We plan to ship our new onboarding flow (5 screens: sign up, verify phone, pick a plan, add a card, welcome) on Friday. The team says everything is fine. Review it and tell me honestly whether it is ready. I can describe each screen if you ask.
evals.expected_output: Runs the release gate review: asks to use the build cold on a real device or says it cannot judge from a description, names the one thing the flow is for, counts steps to first value and challenges each, checks the back of the fence (error, offline, empty, cancel, emails and push texts, the 404), proposes a cut list before a fix list, rates each finding 0-4 with the highest severity first, and ends with a blunt Ship or Not done verdict. States what was not checked.

evals.name: lost-users-orientation
evals.prompt: Support keeps getting the same question: "where do I find my invoices?" Our web app has a left sidebar with 14 items, a settings page and a profile menu. Figure out what is wrong and what to change.
evals.expected_output: Applies the orientation test (where am I, what are my options, how do I get back) and the information-architecture rules: starts from the job (find an invoice) and who does it, not from the menu; severity-rates the finding; fixes the class in the shared layer (grouping by job, search as navigation, a visible path from the places people look first) rather than adding another menu item; proposes a measurable signal for success (fewer where-is-it tickets).

evals.name: flutter-ios-native-idiom
evals.prompt: Our Flutter app looks fine on Android but testers on iPhone say it feels off: the bottom button is half under the home indicator, the back swipe sometimes does nothing, and big text sizes break the layout. Fix the screen scaffold and tell me what to check.
evals.expected_output: Uses SafeArea and MediaQuery padding so nothing interactive sits under the home indicator or Dynamic Island, stops custom gestures from claiming the left-edge swipe-back, scales text with the system (tests the largest step, no fixed heights on text containers), keeps 44 pt targets, mentions dark mode semantic colors, and says that safe areas, gestures and text scaling must be checked on a real iPhone.
